judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The 'Managing Diabetes' link is the title at the start of a bulleted resource-list item ("Start Here"); the item goes on with an NIH badge image, then the source organisation in parentheses (span.desc-text), then "Also in Spanish" on its own line. On the live page (headless Edge, 1280 px) the link is #006699 at 14px with no underline at rest (underline only on hover), but the text next to it is not #444444 at the same size, as the evidence implies: #444444 is the li color, which colors no visible text; the adjacent text is #666666 at 12px. So the link is set apart by a larger font size as well as by color, and is further separated by the badge image and the parentheses. That is exactly G182 example 3 (a list of article links with extra information, links not underlined but in a larger font than the rest), a sufficient technique for 1.4.1; F73 itself says links can be evident from page design and context, and this is a list-item title, not a link inside running text. The rule only counts underline, border, weight, style, icons and pseudo-elements, not font size, so it applied a stricter test than WCAG. (The "Spanish" link in "Also in Spanish" is a closer F73 case, but it is not the element reported here.)

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The search "GO" submit button has white text, 14px bold, which counts as normal-size text (bold large text starts at 18.66px), so it needs 4.5:1. On the live page the hover rule swaps the background to linear-gradient(#329e39 75%, #2b8737 100%), so the whole glyph area (centre of a 38px button) sits on solid #329e39. White on #329e39 is 3.45:1, and there is no text-shadow or other aid. At rest the darker gradient passes. The Understanding document for 1.4.3 says it applies to text shown while a pointer hovers over an object, and no exception (inactive, incidental, logotype) applies. I found no reason the claim fails: real 1.4.3 failure in the hover state.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the "Search MedlinePlus" text input (#searchtext_primary). On focus it gets a Bootstrap-style #66afe9 border and a pale blue glow, with outline none. The probe is right that these are under 3:1 (the #66afe9 border is 2.37:1 on white; the glow is lighter). But this is a text input: when it gets focus it shows the native text caret, which keeps the default color (caret-color auto = #444444, 9.7:1 on the white field). The 1.4.11 Understanding document (Figure 33, "Text input focus style") passes exactly this case: a faint outline under 3:1 plus a visible caret, because the caret is a strong enough focus indication. It fails only when the caret is customised to low contrast (Figure 44), which is not so here. The probe compares screenshots, which normally hide the blinking caret, and then requires the styled ring to reach 3:1 by itself. That is stricter than what the criterion requires.
